rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph interprets Pharaoh’s paired dreams as one vision: the seven healthy cows and full ears signify seven prosperous years.
rows.anchor: الرؤيا يا فرعون واحدة , أطلع الله فرعون على ما هو مزيع أن يفعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven gaunt cows and blighted ears signify seven famine years that consume the stored abundance and threaten the population.
rows.anchor: والسبع بقرات الضعيفات المهزولات اللاتي صعدان بعدهن والسبع سنبلات المهزولات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dream recurred because the matter was fixed before God and its fulfillment would come soon.
rows.anchor: لأن الأمر معد بين يدي الرب , والله معجل فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph advises appointing a wise administrator to collect a fifth during the fertile years and preserve grain in village storehouses for famine.
rows.anchor: فيوليه أرض مصر , فيقاسم أهل مصر على الخمس في السبع السنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh and his servants accept Joseph’s advice, and Pharaoh declares that no one is comparable to him because God revealed the interpretation.
rows.anchor: فحسن هذا القول عند فرعون وعند عبيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh appoints Joseph over Egypt, grants him authority over the people, and honors him with his signet, linen, gold, and a royal chariot.
rows.anchor: انظر فقد وليتك جميع أرض مصر , وخلع فرعون خاتمه من خنصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account gives Joseph’s age as thirty at his audience with Pharaoh and says he toured Egypt after becoming governor.
rows.anchor: وكان قد أتى على يوسف ثلاثون سنة إذ وقف بين يدي فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph stored Egypt’s immense harvest, collecting each village’s grain and an uncountable quantity in its storehouses.
rows.anchor: جمع قمح حقول كل قرية وما أحاط بها فخزنة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s wife is named Asenath, with variant forms for her name and her father’s priestly office and city.
rows.anchor: ولدت له أسنة - وفي نسخة : أسنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph names his first son Manasseh because God made him forget his toil and his father’s household, and the second Ephraim because God made him fruitful.
rows.anchor: إن الله أنساني حميع تعبي - وفي نسخة : شقائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The famine begins as Joseph foretold, bread disappears in Egypt, and Pharaoh directs the people to Joseph for food.
rows.anchor: فكان الجوع في جميع أرض مصر , ولم يوجد الخبز في جميع أرض مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the fertile years, famine covers Egypt and neighboring lands; Joseph releases the stored grain gradually as the wise planner prescribed, drawing buyers from everywhere.
rows.anchor: فأخرج ما كان ادخره من غلال سبع سنين بالتدريج أولا فأولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ten of Joseph’s brothers come to buy grain, while Jacob keeps Benjamin, Joseph’s full brother, at home.
rows.anchor: وجاء إخوة يوسف } العشرة لذلك , وحلف أبوهم بنيامين أخا يوسف عليه السلام لأمه عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph recognizes his brothers because he expects them amid famine and remembers their appearance; they fail to recognize him after a long separation and his changed royal circumstances.
rows.anchor: فعرفهم } لأنه كان مرتقبا لحضورهم لعلمه بجدب بلادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their failure to recognize him also reflects their lack of expectation and the changes in his age, attendants, clothing, country, and royal standing.
rows.anchor: لطول العهد , مع ما تغير عليهم من هيئته بالسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast anticipates the Qur’anic promise that Joseph would later inform them of their deed while they remained unaware.
rows.anchor: وغير ذلك مما ينكر معه المعروف , ويستوحش لأجله من المألوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary links the brothers’ lack of recognition to the earlier promise that Joseph would tell them of their deed while they did not perceive it.
rows.anchor: لتنبئنهم بأمرهم هذا وهم لا يشعرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entering means moving into an enclosed space; recognition is inwardly distinguishing a thing by its defining features.
rows.anchor: والدخول : الانتقال إلى محيط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph questions the brothers about their circumstances, suspects they may be spies, and learns of their father and younger brother as evidence of their situation.
rows.anchor: فطلبوا منه الميرة فباعهم بعد أن استخبرهم عن أمرهم , وقال لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers had come seeking provisions, which Joseph supplies after deciding they are not spies.
rows.anchor: فطلبوا منه الميرة فباعهم بعد أن استخبرهم عن أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jihaz is valuable travel cargo or provisions carried from one place to another.
rows.anchor: والجهاز : فاخر المتاع الذي يحمل من بلد إلى بلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph may require Benjamin either to verify the brothers’ account through their righteous father or to provide the younger brother’s requested share while concealing his disbelief.
rows.anchor: حتى أصدقكم , أو أنهم طلبوا منه لأخيهم حملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph says he gives full measure consistently and is the best host because he places each thing in its most fitting position.
rows.anchor: أني أوفي الكيل } أي أتمه دائما على ما يوجبه الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He warns that without Benjamin they will receive no further measure and may not approach him.
rows.anchor: فإن لم تأتوني به } أي بأخيكم أول قدمة تقدمونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers promise to plead, bargain, and gently persuade their father, then emphasize in an emphatic nominal sentence that they will do it.
rows.anchor: قالوا سنراود } أي بوعد لا خلف فيه حين نصل { عن أباه } أي نكلمه فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of raawada turns on circling or turning, with associated senses of intent, approach, departure, gentleness, and delay; the commentary refers back to its earlier treatment.
rows.anchor: وقد مضى عند { وراودته } أن المادة - يائية وواوية بهمز وبغير همز -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamzated root darʾ centers on pushing or repelling, yielding senses such as dispute, sudden appearance, protrusion, and force.
rows.anchor: درأ علينا , أي خرج مفاجأة , قال القزاز

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzaz explains the phrase about floodwater coming in succession as a sudden arrival from an unknown place.
rows.anchor: قال القزاز : وأصله من قولهم : جاء السيل درأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary derives diverse forms concerning swelling, shining stars, spreading fire, bending paths, and rising or protruding features from the underlying idea of pushing.
rows.anchor: والدرء : النشوز , وهو من الدفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The related r-d-ʾ family includes supporting or assisting someone, bracing a wall, and throwing something that pushes its target.
rows.anchor: والردء : العون والمادة والعدل الثقيل - لأنه يدافع ليعتدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source groups trembling, agitation, height, and bodily motion under the associated notion of things pushing against one another.
rows.anchor: والريح : اضطربت - فكأن بعضها يدفع بعضا

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzaz describes raʾida as a quick-growing young woman with good nourishment and gives related senses for soft or trembling movement.
rows.anchor: وقال القزاز : السريعة الشباب مع حسن غذاء

rows.speaker: ابن دريد
rows.claim: Ibn Durayd distinguishes unhamzated raʾida, a girl who comes and goes often, from hamzated ruʾda, a soft, graceful girl.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن دريد : جارية رأدة - غير مهموز : كثيرة المجيء والذهاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph orders his servants—young, strong attendants—to return the brothers’ payment, the money they had tendered for their food, to their travel bags.
rows.anchor: وأصل الفتى : الشاب القوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahl refers to a container or mount prepared for a journey; the returned payment is placed in the brothers’ baggage.
rows.anchor: والرحل : ما أعد للرحيل من وعاء أو مركب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s wording about their recognizing the returned money expresses optimistic confidence, probability, or knowledge by revelation.
rows.anchor: وعبر بأداة التحقق تفاؤلا لهم بالسلامة , أو ظنا , أو علما بالوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He hopes recognition will prompt them to return it scrupulously, return for provisions if they lack funds, or come back in hope of similar generosity.
rows.anchor: لردها تورعا , أو للميرة بها إن لم يكن عندهم غيرها , أو طمعا في مثل هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph does not identify himself immediately because the coming events and divine planning make that impossible under the circumstances.
rows.anchor: لأن ذلك غير ممكن عادة - لما يأتي من الحكم البالغة والتدبير المتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers return quickly, motivated by the Egyptian governor’s kindness and their need for more provisions.
rows.anchor: حملهم ما رأوا - من إحسان الصديق وحاجتهم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers say Benjamin’s absence caused them to be denied his camel’s measure and warn that all will be denied next time unless they bring him.
rows.anchor: منع منا الكيل } لأخينا بنيامين على بعيره لغيبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read the verb with second-person yāʾ, meaning each brother will take his own measure; the majority read it with first-person nūn.
rows.anchor: هذا على قراءة حمزة والكسائي بالتحانية , ولنؤوله على قراءة الجماعة بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers renew their promise to protect Benjamin because their earlier treatment of Joseph gives Jacob reason to distrust them.
rows.anchor: وأكدوا لما تقدم من فعلهم بيوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام مما يوجب الارتياب بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob questions whether he can trust them after their failure to protect Joseph, whose return they had previously guaranteed.
rows.anchor: قال هل آمنكم } أي أقبل منكم الآن وفي مستقبل الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s settled reliance is on God as the best protector, more merciful to him than to let him lose Benjamin after Joseph.
rows.anchor: فالله } أي المحيط علما وقدرة { خير حافظا } منكم ومن كل أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers discover that the money they brought from Canaan to buy food has been returned in their baggage.
rows.anchor: وجدوا بضاعتهم } أي ما كان معهم من كنعان بشراء القوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They argue that the returned payment confirms their honorable treatment and gives them a reason to return, provision their family, and bring Benjamin safely.
rows.anchor: هذه بضاعتنا } ثم بينوا مضمون الإشارة بقولهم : { ردت إلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised extra measure is explained as a twelfth camel-load: one for each brother and an additional share for the detained brother on the two visits; the source says the first grant was nine loads.
rows.anchor: فيكون جملة ما نأتي به بعد الرجوع إليه اثني عشر حملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary invokes the Torah’s account that one brother was imprisoned so the others would bring their younger brother.
rows.anchor: ويدل على ما في التوراة - من أنه كان سجن أحدهم ليأتوا بأخيهم الأصغر - قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call the extra amount an easy measure compared with the governor’s generosity, wealth, and ambition.
rows.anchor: { ذلك كيل يسير * } بالنسبة إلى ما رأينا من كرم شمائله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob refuses to send Benjamin until the sons give a solemn covenant by God that they will bring him back.
rows.anchor: لن أرسله } أي بنيامين كائنا { معكم } أي في وقت من الأوقات { حتى تؤتون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception for being overwhelmed means a calamity beyond their control that destroys them all; Jacob’s grief over Joseph motivates his insistence.
rows.anchor: إلا } في حال { أي يحاط } أي تحصل الإحاطة بمصيبة من المصائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob combines taking practical precautions with reliance on God, then declares God the trustee over their agreement and able to fulfill it.
rows.anchor: وهذا من باب { اعقلها وتوكل } فأجابوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob tells the eleven handsome, conspicuous brothers to enter through widely separated gates to guard against envy and the evil eye; they had been unknown on the first journey.
rows.anchor: أحد عشر رجلا إخوة أهل جمال وبسطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rummani transmits from Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi that Jacob’s instruction was a precaution against the evil eye.
rows.anchor: كما نقله الرماني عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما والحسن وقتادة والضحاك والسدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil eye is real but itself part of divine destiny; prophetic reports support taking precautions.
rows.anchor: فإن العين حق , وهي من قدر الله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet’s statement that the evil eye is real; the commentary says this appears in both Sahih collections and elsewhere.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ( العين حق )

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: A report in Ahmad and Ibn Majah adds that Satan’s presence and human envy accompany the evil eye.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عند أحمد وابن ماجه : ( يحضرها الشيطان وحسد بن آدم )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
rows.claim: A report in Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasaʾi says the eye is real, could precede destiny if anything could, and calls for washing when requested.
rows.anchor: ولمسلم والترمذي والنسائي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: جابر رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: A report in Abu Nuʿaym’s Hilya says the evil eye can send a camel into a pot and a man to the grave.
rows.anchor: ولأبي نعيم في الحيلة عن جابر رضي الله عنه أن النبي قال : ( إن العين لتدخل الجمل القدر

rows.speaker: أسماء بنت يزيد رضي الله عنها
rows.claim: A report in Abu Dawud says the evil eye can overtake a rider and make him fall.
rows.anchor: ولأبي داود عن أسماء بنت يزيد رضي الله عنها أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أسماء بنت عميس رضي الله عنها
rows.claim: A report in Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi says that if anything could precede destiny, it would be the evil eye.
rows.anchor: ولأحمد والترمذي عن أسماء بنت عميس رضي الله عنها أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi explains the evil eye as arising from an evil soul imagining the destruction of the person it affects.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام الرازي : ومنشأ إصابة العين توهم النفس الخبيثة هلاك من تصيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Caution is taking commanded means that belong to divine destiny, not trying to escape destiny; the strong believer should pursue benefit, seek God’s help, and avoid helplessness and regretful what-ifs.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاحتياط من باب الأخذ بالأسباب المأمور بها , لأنها من القدر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: A report in Muslim, Ahmad, and Ibn Majah says the strong believer is better and more beloved to God, urges useful effort with divine help, and rejects counterfactual regret after misfortune.
rows.anchor: كما روى مسلم وأحمد وابن ماجه عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( المؤمن القوي خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains the report as careful attention to possible benefits and harms, followed by acceptance of God’s decree when events differ from one’s aims.
rows.anchor: افعل فعل الأقوياء , ولا تفعل فعل العجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob denies that precautions can shield his sons from any divine decision and clarifies that God alone governs every outcome.
rows.anchor: فقال : { وما أغني } أي أجزي وأسد وأنوب { عنكم من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase that judgment belongs to God means no one can escape what God wills; causes work only if God allows them to do so.
rows.anchor: ثم علل ذلك بقوله : { إن } أي ما { الحكم } وهو فصل الأمر

rows.speaker: علي ابن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Abu Nuʿaym through al-Shafiʿi attributes to Ali sayings that destiny is a deep sea, a dark house, and God’s secret, which one should not probe.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو نعيم في الحيلة في ترجمة إمامنا الشافعي بسنده إليه ثم إلى علي ابن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: علي ابن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: In the same report, Ali describes human responsibility as between compulsion and unrestricted delegation, and says capacity is possessed through God if He grants it.
rows.anchor: أما إذا أبيت فإنه أمر بين أمرين , لا جبر ولا تفويض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God alone rules all matters, Jacob entrusts himself to Him and commands steadfast believers to trust Him, a duty whose fulfillment brings success.
rows.anchor: عليه } أي على الله وحده الذي ليس الحكم إلا له { توكلت } أي جعلته وكيلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers do not hurry back on this trip, since the moment calls for gentleness and they need not imply they are replacing exhausted provisions.
rows.anchor: والزمان زمان رفق , لا زمان تبسط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their entering through separate gates did not avert God’s later trial of accusation and Benjamin’s detention; it fulfilled Jacob’s desire that they obey his precaution.
rows.anchor: إلا حاجة } أي شيئا غير أتم حاجة { في نفس يعقوب

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan cites the verse as evidence that لما is a particle expressing one event’s necessary consequence, not a temporal adverb, because of its position after negation.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : وفيه حجة لمن زعم أن ( لما ) حرف وجوب لوجوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God praises Jacob’s knowledge to encourage practical precautions alongside belief that outcomes remain in God’s hands.
rows.anchor: أشار تعالى إلى رده بمدح يعقوب عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s knowledge comes from God’s teaching and encompasses both religious commands and divine determination; لما علمناه can mean what God taught him or because God taught him.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى : لذو علم لأجل تعليمنا إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may be connected; treating it as disconnected still honors Jacob by presenting his action as worthy of averting harm because it followed God’s direction.
rows.anchor: يتبين أن الاستثناء متصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author glosses yughni as repel because the root gh-n-y, in any arrangement, centers on remaining or residence.
rows.anchor: وإنما فسرت ( يغنى ) ب ( يدفع ) لأن مادة ( غنى ) - بأي ترتيب كان - تدور على الإقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of يغني is associated with staying or residing; by extension, being sufficient, replacing someone, or removing and repelling a burden.
rows.anchor: وأغنى عنه غناء فلان : ناب عنه منابه وأجزأ مجزأه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary traces related forms for settlement, wealth, singing, conversation, and news to ideas of remaining, satisfying, or calming the mind.
rows.anchor: ويلزم أيضا - من الإقامة التي هي المدار والكفاية التي هي سببها - الغناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It further links derivatives for dwelling places, covered hearts, vegetation, and bodily conditions to the same semantic field of remaining or covering.
rows.anchor: والغين : الغيم - لإقامته في الهواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion concludes that ordinary people lack the divinely taught knowledge Jacob possesses because worldly concerns and appetites distract them from sound nature.
rows.anchor: لإعراضهم عنه واستفرغ قواهم في الاهتمام بما وقع التكفل لهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph welcomes Benjamin as his full brother; he had each of the other brothers dine in pairs, leaving Benjamin alone, so he invited him to dine with himself.
rows.anchor: فبقي بنيامين بلا ثان , فقال : هذا يأكل معي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrangement of separate dining places mirrors Jacob’s earlier instruction to enter through separate gates.
rows.anchor: وهذا التفريق موافق لما أمرهم به أبوهم في تفريق الدخول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph privately identifies himself to Benjamin because there is no reason to conceal it from him; he comforts him about the brothers’ past conduct.
rows.anchor: قال } معلما له , لأنه لا سبب يقتضي الكتم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awa means drawing someone close into a place of rest, while tabtaʾis means to acquire grief or distress.
rows.anchor: والإيواء : ضم النفس بالتصيير إلى موضع الراحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph quickly and carefully provisions the brothers so he can get private time with Benjamin and implement his plan without a witness.
rows.anchor: وأسرع في تجهيزهم في هذه المرة قصدا إلى انفراده بأخيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drinking vessel is Joseph’s own water cup, which he secretly places in Benjamin’s baggage to keep his brother with him.
rows.anchor: { السقاية } التي له . وهي إناء يسقي به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s stratagem carries the risk of a less perceptive observer judging Benjamin a thief, but the near-term benefits justify the lesser harm and Benjamin’s innocence will soon be clear.
rows.anchor: فهو من باب ارتكاب أخف الضررين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary says the brothers are allowed to leave before a herald summons them and accuses the caravan of theft.
rows.anchor: ثم أمهلهم حتى انطلقوا , ثم أرسل إليهم فحبسوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The absence of a vocative particle conveys closeness despite the herald’s loud call; ʿayr means the people of a caravan, originally associated with donkeys.
rows.anchor: أيتها العير } أي أهلها , وأكد لما لهم من الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph may not have ordered the accusation: the herald could have inferred it from an instruction that the vessel was with the caravan.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن لا يكون بأمره حتى يحتاج إلى تصحيحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural accusation attributes the act to the whole group by their consent even though one individual took the vessel.
rows.anchor: وإفراد الضمير تارة وجمعه أخرى دليل على أن القاتل واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative says the brothers turn back and ask their pursuers directly what is missing, rather than rushing to deny an unspecified charge.
rows.anchor: { ماذا تفقدون * } مما يمكننا أخذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The herald identifies the missing object as the king’s drinking cup and promises a camel-load to whoever returns it; zaʿim means guarantor.
rows.anchor: والصواع : الجام يشرب فيه { ولمن جاء به } أي أظهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haml with kasra is cargo carried on the back, whereas haml with fatha is a burden carried in the womb.
rows.anchor: وهو بالكسر : قدر من المتاع مهيأ لأن يحمل على الظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode illustrates achieving a rightful aim through tactful outward appearances and a truthful hidden plan.
rows.anchor: من إيقاع الأسباب التي تؤدي إليه وتبعث عليه بظاهر جميل وباطن حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers swear by God that the Egyptians already know they did not come to corrupt the land or steal, citing their trustworthy conduct, including returning their payment.
rows.anchor: ما جئنا } وأكدوا النفي باللام فقالوا : { لنفسد } أي نوقع الفساد { وفي الأرض و } لقد علمتم { ما كنا } أي بوجه من الوجوه { سارقين *

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taʾ in tالله is an uncommon oath form; al-Rummani says its rarity made it apt for expressing an unusual or astonishing meaning and relates it to waw and baʾ.
rows.anchor: قال الرماني : لأنها لما كانت نادرة في أدوات القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The officials, confident the vessel is among the brothers, ask what penalty applies if their denial proves false; jazāʾ means recompense corresponding to an act.
rows.anchor: والجزاء : مقابلة العمل بما يستحق عليه من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers state that whoever has the vessel found in his baggage will be the penalty, framing liability around discovery rather than proving theft.
rows.anchor: ولما كان العبرة بنفس الوجدان , بنوا للمفعول قولهم : { وجد في رحله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their repeated formulation presents this as their established practice: they punish wrongdoers as thieves.
rows.anchor: ثم أكدوا ذلك بقولهم : { فهو جزاءه } أي ليس غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The search begins with the other brothers’ containers and reaches Benjamin’s only after them, distancing the procedure from suspicion of a setup.
rows.anchor: فبدأ } أي فتسبب عن ذلك أنه بدأ المؤذن أو غيره ممن أمر بذلك { بأوعيتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s plan lets Joseph retain Benjamin under the brothers’ own legal rule, requiting their former plot against Joseph and using their judgment against themselves.
rows.anchor: كذلك } أي مثل هذا الكيد العظيم { كدنا ليوسف } خاصة بأن علمناه إياه جزاء لهم على كيدهم بيوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Egyptian royal law would not permit Joseph to take Benjamin for theft, so he could do so only through a cause God willed, such as their self-imposed penalty.
rows.anchor: في دين الملك } يعني ملك مصر , على حالة من الحالات , لأن جزاء السارق عندهم غير هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary relates the forms of s-r-q, s-q-r, q-s-r, and q-r-s to painful or forceful overpowering, sometimes accompanied by concealment, weakness, heat, or cold.
rows.anchor: ومادة ( سرق ) بتراكيبها الأربعة : سرق , وسقر , وقسر , وقرس - تدور على الغلبة المحرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root survey associates qasr and related words with domination, lions, hunters, strong youths, and the concealed pursuit of prey.
rows.anchor: فمن مطلق الغلبة : القسر , وهو الغلبة والقهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary describes stealing as taking secretly or by trick and links the root to hidden listeners and furtive departure.
rows.anchor: ومنه السرق , وهوالأخذ في خفية , وعبارة القزاز : في ختل وغفلة

rows.speaker: ابن دريد
rows.claim: Ibn Durayd defines q-s-r as taking by force and oppression.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن دريد : القسر : الأخذ بالغلبة والاضظهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qaswara and qasur forms denote a lion, hunter, or strong youth, consistent with the root idea of overpowering.
rows.anchor: والقسورة : الأسد , والعزيز كالقسور , والرماة من الصيادين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extended lexical discussion connects secret taking with weakness and furtiveness, and compares related words for old age, shortness, silk, and painful heat or cold.
rows.anchor: إذا تقرر ذلك فتصحيح قول المؤذن ( إنكم لسارقون )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The herald’s accusation is justified literally if it recalls the brothers’ secret seizure of Joseph; otherwise it is figurative because they unknowingly carry another’s property and act like thieves.
rows.anchor: إن نظرإلى الغلبة في خفاء فلا شك أنهم متصفون بذلك لأخذهم يوسف من أبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary supports the literal reading with the promise that Joseph would tell them of their deed while they were unaware, and the figurative reading with the later wording about finding the goods with someone.
rows.anchor: ويقوي إرادة الأول قوله تعالى { لتنبئهم بأمرهم هذا وهم لا يشعرون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s elevation from humiliation to authority is presented as God’s raising of degrees, using a cause that defeats the brothers’ efforts to lower him.
rows.anchor: فقال تعالى - التفاتا إلى مقام التكلم تقوية للكلام بمقام الغيبة والتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one above every human knower is God, whose knowledge can set causes in motion that confound even the learned.
rows.anchor: { وفوق كل ذي علم } أي من الخلق { عليم } عظيم العلم

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani reports from Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and Saʿid ibn Jubayr that God is the knower above every possessor of knowledge.
rows.anchor: كما نقله الرماني عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما والحسن وسعيد بن جبيرن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers avoid directly asserting Benjamin’s theft: trusting his honesty, they suspect the cup was planted as their own payment had been, though his silence weakens that explanation.
rows.anchor: { إن يسرق } فلم يجزموا بسرقتهن لعلهم بأمانته , وظنهم هذا الصواع دس في رحله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed report says Benjamin rebuked them, saying they had placed the cup in his bag as they had placed their payment in the others’ bags.
rows.anchor: على أنه قد ورد أنهم لامواه فقال لهم : وضعه في رحلي الذي وضع البضاعة في رحالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed account says Joseph’s maternal aunt hid Isaac’s belt on him and then claimed it missing, so Jacob allowed Joseph to stay with her when it was found.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنه قيل : إن عمته كانت لا تصبر عنه , وكان أبوه لا يسمح بمكثه عندها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers’ accusation recalls that alleged episode: Joseph’s maternal aunt found her father’s belt under his clothes and kept him with her.
rows.anchor: فحزمته من تحت ثيابه بمنظقة أبيها إسحاق عليه السلام وكانت عندها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph keeps his response to their insult inside because he is now able to take revenge, but he does not reveal the insult to them.
rows.anchor: فأسرها } أي إجابتهم عن هذه القولة القبيحة { يوسف في نفسه } على تمكنه مما يريد بهم من الانتقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He considers them worse because their harm to Joseph was deliberate, whereas what happened to him and Benjamin served a beneficial outcome; Allah knows their false description.
rows.anchor: قال أنتم شر مكانا } أي من يوسف وأخيه , لأن ما نس إليهما من الشر إنما هو ظاهرا لأمر خير اقتضاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Place denotes the brothers’ moral condition; Joseph delays mentioning the judgment he kept private so they will not hear his condemnation.
rows.anchor: ونسبة الشر إلى مكانهم أعظم من نسبته إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasf is a word derived from a root that distinguishes its referent from other things, as in distinguishing knowledgeable from ignorant.
rows.anchor: والوصف : كلمة مشتقة من أصل من الأصول لتجري على مذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers appeal to the ruler’s status and kindness, describing their elderly, deeply attached father and offering one of themselves in Benjamin’s place.
rows.anchor: إن له أبا شيخا كبيرا فخذ أحدنا مكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call Joseph a benefactor and ask him to act according to the generosity they believe they have witnessed.
rows.anchor: نا نراك } أي نعلمك علما هو كالرؤية أو بحسب ما رأيناه { من المحسنين * } أي العريقين في صفة الإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph seeks refuge in God from taking anyone except the person whose baggage contains the vessel, avoiding the unsupported charge that Benjamin stole it.
rows.anchor: أن نأخذ } أي لأجل هذا الأمر { إلا من } أي الشخص الذي { وجدنا متاعنا عنده }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph says taking a substitute would make them unjust under their own law, since Benjamin alone was found with the king’s property.
rows.anchor: { إنا إذا } أي أخذنا أحدا مكانه { لظالمون * } أي عريقون في الظلم في دينكم

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah narrative describes famine and unrest across the earth; Joseph opens the granaries and sells grain to Egyptians and people arriving from other lands.
rows.anchor: وكان القهم - وفي نسخة : الجوع - والإرجاف على جميع وجه الأرض

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: Jacob sends ten sons to Egypt after hearing there is grain, while keeping Benjamin home because he fears some misfortune might befall him.
rows.anchor: فهبط بنو يعقوب عليه الصلاة والسلام العشرة ليمتاروا ميرة من مصر

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah account says Joseph governs the land and distributes food; his brothers arrive, bow, and he recognizes them while pretending not to know them.
rows.anchor: وكان يوسف هو المسلط على الأرض , وكان يميز جميع شعب الأرض

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: Joseph treats them harshly, asks where they came from, and accuses them of spying; they deny it and present themselves as honest brothers from one family.
rows.anchor: فذكر يوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام الرؤيا التي قصها عليهم وقال لهم : إنكم جواسيس

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The brothers say they are twelve sons of one father: one remains with him and one is missing; Joseph swears by Pharaoh that they will not leave until the youngest arrives.
rows.anchor: نحن اثنا عشر رجلا إخوة عبيدك بنو رجل واحد بأرض كنعان
